fatal_errors: The hypothesis attributes lattice distortion specifically to short-range chemical order, whereas the target mechanism concerns composition-dependent mean-square atomic displacement in homogenized solid solutions; short-range order was not established as its origin.
It assumes annealing followed by quenching will reduce short-range order, but annealing can increase, decrease, or alter ordering depending on temperature and kinetics.
The as-cast versus annealed comparison confounds ordering with segregation, porosity, residual stress, dislocation density, grain structure, and precipitation.
No prior evidence is cited or supplied.
The proposed room-temperature tensile comparison cannot test the target cryogenic inertial dulling or elevated-temperature Portevin-Le Chatelier mechanisms.
explanation: The response addresses the broad idea that local atomic environments impede dislocations, giving limited conceptual overlap with lattice-distortion-controlled solid-solution strengthening. However, it reconstructs neither the homogenized FCC single-crystal system nor the temperature-dependent compression, strain-rate-jump, TEM, and DFT comparison. It omits the distinct governing regimes: thermally activated glide and phonon-drag-controlled inertia at cryogenic temperatures, MSAD scaling of extrapolated 0 K CRSS, and Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell-type dynamic pinning at high temperature. Its proposed experiment could test an ordering-strength relationship if ordering were independently quantified, but the thermal treatment is highly confounded and the asserted direction of ordering change is not justified. Consequently, it is not a supported alternative to the target mechanism.
